output_json.patch_notes: FileUtil.java: replaced the naive startsWith(dir.getCanonicalPath()) containment check with a boundary-aware check that compares canonicalTarget against canonicalDir exactly, or against canonicalDir + File.separator, before extracting each JAR entry. This rejects sibling-directory prefix bypasses (e.g. base "/out" vs escape "/out_evil") while still allowing legitimate entries inside the extraction directory.\n\nFileUtilTest.java: added siblingPrefixEscapeTest, a regression test that builds a JAR containing entry "../test_evil/pwned.txt" and asserts FileUtil.unjar throws and that the sibling escape file is never created. Existing goodExtractTest and badExtractTest still pass.
output_json.risk_notes: Low risk. The change only tightens the existing containment guard; legitimate entries that resolve inside the extraction directory (verified by goodExtractTest) still extract normally. The equals() clause preserves the edge case where an entry resolves to the extraction directory itself. Behavior for absolute-path entries and plain "../" traversal is unchanged. No API, dependency, or formatting changes beyond the guard and the added test.
output_json.summary: Fixed a path-traversal (CWE-022) in FileUtil.unjar's destination-containment guard. The original check used target.getCanonicalPath().startsWith(dir.getCanonicalPath()) without a trailing separator, so a JAR entry like "../out_evil/pwned.txt" whose canonical path is a sibling directory ("<base>/out_evil") sharing the string prefix of the extraction dir ("<base>/out") passed the check and was written outside the intended directory. The guard now requires the canonical target to equal the canonical dir or start with canonicalDir + File.separator, closing the prefix bypass.
